context: Questions about two public Go libraries whose GitHub issues and pull requests are in the graph: jackc/puddle, a resource pool, and tidwall/btree, a B-tree.

questions.question: Why could Pool.CreateResource deadlock, and has it been fixed?
questions.context: Issues and pull requests of jackc/puddle, a resource pool library for Go.

facts.fact: It deadlocks when the pool is closed while a resource is being acquired, because the lock is not released after the closed check.

stated.quote: the lock on `p.cond.L` is not released after checking `p.closed` and returning `ErrClosedPool`

facts.fact: A pull request fixes the deadlock.

stated.quote: Fixes a deadlock in Pool.CreateResource

questions.note: Run by hand on 2026-11-12, with this context.

questions.question: What problem was the pull request that uses atomic operations to avoid locking written to solve?

facts.fact: The pull request was written for issue 17.

stated.quote: related to GitHub issue https://github.com/jackc/puddle/issues/17
For this issue

facts.fact: Acquire did not return at once when its context was done, because it took a lock first.

stated.quote: does not return immediately when ctx.Done() is called due to a lock attempt before returning

questions.note: Run by hand on 2026-11-12.

questions.question: A released resource was sitting unused while the goroutine that released it kept running. What was done about it?

facts.fact: runtime.Gosched() is called after the semaphore is released, when a goroutine is blocked in Acquire.

stated.quote: adding `runtime.Gosched()` after semaphore release in `Release`, `Destroy`, and `Hijack` functions, only when a goroutine is blocked in `Acquire`

facts.fact: The problem: a released resource stays unusable while the releasing goroutine keeps running.

stated.quote: a released resource stays unusable for as long as the releasing goroutine keeps running

questions.question: Under contention, how long does a resource that has just been released go unused, and what does that do to throughput?

facts.fact: Throughput drops by a third.

questions.question: What sequence of iterator calls makes IterG.Prev go on returning true past the start of the tree?

facts.fact: Last, then Next, then Prev beyond the far end.

stated.quote: when `Last` is called, followed by `Next`, and then `Prev` is called beyond the far end

questions.question: Does DeleteHint make any use of the hint it is passed?

facts.fact: No: it passes nil in place of the hint, so it behaves like Delete.

stated.quote: passing nil instead of the provided hint

questions.question: Where in the tree's binary search could an integer overflow, and how does Go's own library avoid it?

facts.fact: The midpoint is computed as (low + high) / 2.

stated.quote: risks integer overflow due to (low + high) / 2

facts.fact: The standard library computes int(uint(i+j) >> 1).

stated.quote: int(uint(i+j) >> 1)
